classification.difficultyReason: Read the mean, signed amplitude and period from four supplied transformed sine and cosine graphs.

content.prompt: Find the values of $a$, $b$ and $n$ for each graph.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The graph of $y=b+a\sin nx$ is shown below.

spec.description: Two sine cycles, starting at the mean and rising; labelled axes, four x ticks and three dashed horizontal guides.
spec.mathematics: Domain 0 to 4π; maximum 3, minimum −1, mean 1, period 2π.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is always visible; its equation and parameter values are not printed on the graph.

answer.worked:
The graph starts at its mean and rises, so $a$ is positive.
$$\begin{align*}b&=\frac{3+(-1)}{2}=1\\a&=\frac{3-(-1)}{2}=2\end{align*}$$
The period is $2\pi$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2\pi}{n}&=2\pi\\n&=1\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The graph of $y=b+a\cos nx$ is shown below.

spec.description: One reflected cosine cycle; x labels above the axis, dashed guides at 5 and −5.
spec.mathematics: Domain 0 to 12; minimum −5 at both endpoints, maximum 5 at x=6, zeros at 3 and 9.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is always visible; parameter values remain answer content.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}b&=\frac{5+(-5)}{2}=0\\|a|&=\frac{5-(-5)}{2}=5\end{align*}$$
The cosine graph starts at its minimum, so $a=-5$. The period is $12$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2\pi}{n}&=12\\12n&=2\pi\\n&=\frac{\pi}{6}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The graph of $y=b+a\sin nx$ is shown below.

spec.description: Two reflected sine cycles starting at the mean and falling; fraction-labelled x ticks and dashed guides at 2, 4 and 6.
spec.mathematics: Domain 0 to 4/3; mean 4, amplitude 2, period 2/3; minima at 1/6 and 5/6, maxima at 1/2 and 7/6.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph is visible without its equation or parameter values.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}b&=\frac{6+2}{2}=4\\|a|&=\frac{6-2}{2}=2\end{align*}$$
The graph starts at its mean and falls, so $a=-2$. Two cycles occupy an interval of length $\frac{4}{3}$, giving period $\frac{2}{3}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2\pi}{n}&=\frac{2}{3}\\2n&=6\pi\\n&=3\pi\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The graph of $y=b+a\cos nx$ is shown below.

spec.description: Cosine curve starting at its maximum; dashed maximum guide, labelled zero, and four fraction/multiple-of-π x ticks.
spec.mathematics: Domain 0 to π; maximum 3 at 0 and 2π/3; minimum 0 at π/3 and π; period 2π/3.
spec.answerVisibility: Given extrema and ticks remain visible; derived mean, amplitude and frequency remain answer content.

answer.worked:
The cosine graph starts at its maximum, so $a$ is positive.
$$\begin{align*}b&=\frac{3+0}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\\a&=\frac{3-0}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\end{align*}$$
The period is $\frac{2\pi}{3}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2\pi}{n}&=\frac{2\pi}{3}\\n&=3\end{align*}$$
